@mihe The [documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/physics/using_jolt_physics.html#area3d-and-softbody3d) implies that overlap events should be triggered by soft bodies on areas as well. I tried to create a repro case for this, but I've come to the conclusion that GodotPhysics doesn't support this either. I've added body entered/exited handlers to the MRP but these don't trigger.

When an overlap is detected we start here:

```
GodotAreaSoftBodyPair3D::pre_solve(float p_step) Line 249
GodotStep3D::_pre_solve_island(LocalVector<GodotConstraint3D *,unsigned int,0,0> & p_constraint_island) Line 125
GodotStep3D::step(GodotSpace3D * p_space, float p_delta) Line 360
GodotPhysicsServer3D::step(float p_step) Line 1685
PhysicsServer3DWrapMT::step(float p_step) Line 62
...
```

Specifically in this section of the code:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/084d5d407e62efcd5be9de44148c5dedce3b9386/modules/godot_physics_3d/godot_area_pair_3d.cpp#L69-L76

It will first go to `GodotSoftBody3D::add_area` which will add the object to the `areas` member. This is only used in `GodotSoftBody3D::predict_motion` to apply the gravity and wind overrides (and we should replicate this in the Jolt module).

Then it will call `GodotArea3D::add_soft_body_to_query` which will add the soft body to the `monitored_soft_bodies`. However, this list could simply be removed as it is not used by anything. `GodotArea3D::call_queries` only loops over `monitored_bodies` and `monitored_areas` lists to fire signals.

Am I missing something?

> The [documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/physics/using_jolt_physics.html#area3d-and-softbody3d) implies that overlap events should be triggered by soft bodies on areas as well. I tried to create a repro case for this, but I've come to the conclusion that GodotPhysics doesn't support this either.

Yeah, I was frankly a bit surprised when reading that part as well yesterday. I seemed to remember `SoftBody3D` not in fact supporting that in Godot Physics, so I'm not sure where that came from.

Looking at the code you pointed to (specifically `GodotArea3D::monitored_soft_bodies`) it seems pretty clear-cut that it does not in fact support that, so I think we can safely remove that part from the documentation.

> I think we can safely remove that part from the documentation.

I put up a pull request to remove it: godotengine/godot-docs#11413

I've been chipping away at this for a little bit now, and have at least gotten the whole contact-to-area pipeline set up, loosely based on the stuff you did ages ago @jrouwe: #114198

What's left to do is porting this code over in some way:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/551ce8d47feda9c81c870314745366b24957624b/modules/godot_physics_3d/godot_soft_body_3d.cpp#L952-L1004

... but I ran out of time, and likely won't be able to resume this for the next few weeks at least:
@mihe shall I have a go at completing this?
@jrouwe You're more than welcome to!

@mihe I understand now why you didn't want to do this, the godot physics implementation has several issues that needed sorting out :)

I've created an implementation here: https://github.com/jrouwe/godot/tree/114198_v2. Note that I rebased your change on latest godot before I started working.

My test project: [soft-body-vs-sensor.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24682241/soft-body-vs-sensor.zip)

Things I ran into for `Area3D`:

* The `Force Magnitude` attribute should actually be named `Pressure` because it is Force / Area. I'm not changing this for compatibility reasons.
* The `Source Path` attribute (which results in wind source and direction) uses the local transform (based on what I see happening in the debugger, code [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/741fb8a30687d0662ab6b5c04a2a531440dd29d9/scene/3d/physics/area_3d.cpp#L178)). Anything you link that's not at the root of the node tree won't work. Again, not changing this for compat reasons.
* The `Attenuation Factor` attribute is completely broken in godot physics. If the object is on the negative side of the source then we're doing pow(negative value, negative value) which results in a NaN and immediate explosion of the sim (my test project above illustrates this). Also, it can amplify the force by ridiculous values when the object is close to the source, resulting in immediate instability. I left this as is for godot but I forbid amplification and avoid NaN's in the jolt module.
* Instead of using the rest area to calculate the pressure on a face, I'm using the actual area. This differs from godot physics, but I feel it is more accurate.

Things I ran into for `SoftBody3D`:

* The default value for `mass` was 0, this was implemented as giving all particles a mass of 1 where godot gives all particles a combined mass of 1. This meant that the wind force had virtually no effect in the jolt module. I've changed this so that it behaves like godot physics with the same error when you try to set a negative mass. In godot physics it is possible to set a mass of 0 but that would cause the sim to explode immediately, so I'm not allowing this in the jolt module. This is a breaking change for the jolt module, but I feel it's justified as it brings it towards godot physics.
* I implemented the gravity override feature for the jolt module by copy pasting the godot physics code. ~~It uses the same `get_transform` function to get the transform. Does this also mean that it is using a local space transform as a world transform?~~

If you agree with these changes, can you merge it into this PR?

> As of writing this, this PR makes it so that the area's overlap signals are emitted whenever a soft body enters/exit its shapes, which is not something Godot Physics supports to begin with, and might perhaps be considered a breaking change (and thus undesirable) as the node passed to the area's body_* signals would not necessarily be a PhysicsBody3D anymore.

Should we add a project option to opt out of area callbacks for soft bodies so that people who run into problems can turn the callbacks off? (I can do this if you want)

Edit: I've updated the branch
1. There was a missing call to `_update_mass` that prevented on the fly mass changes (was already a problem before this change)
2. I found that the position passed to the gravity calculation was indeed wrong as `get_transform` always returns identity.

@mihe, let me know if you don't have time to merge this into your PR. I can also create a new PR with our combined changes. With the release of 4.6 now seems like a good time to get changes like this in the build.

Also let me know if I should make a project setting.

I'll try to get it in this week. I need to sit down and go through your changes either way.

I'm torn on the project setting though. On the one hand there's already precedent for types other than `PhysicsBody3D` being passed into those signals, since things like `GridMap` can also trigger them. On the other hand those signals would now be invoked at times where they previously weren't, so can change game logic unexpectedly.

But... you'd still (kinda) have some recourse/workaround to get back to the old behavior, since you can change the collision layers/masks to prevent those interactions entirely, so I feel like it's not *that* bad so long as we label it as a breaking change in the release notes.

@jrouwe I've pushed your changes to the PR, along with a few other changes, like simplifying some gravity stuff, now that things are more consistent between rigid and soft bodies.

However, changing the total mass of all particles to 1 (which I'll admit I forgot I had diverged from to begin with) is having a somewhat drastic impact on more subdivided meshes, presumably because of the now much smaller per-particle mass. You can see this prominently in the `3d/soft_body_physics` demo project found [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/3d/soft_body_physics).

Note that this demo was seemingly created with the Jolt integration's current behavior in mind, so I wouldn't expect it to be well-behaved with Godot Physics. It's possible that we just need to change the demo a bit, by either increasing the total mass or reducing the subdivision a bit.

However, you can also just crank up the subdivision of the sphere/ball in your test project to something like 30 radial segments and 30 rings, and it'll look like this with a default total mass of 1 kg:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76c7e8a8-00a6-4608-b041-f9fb5c4bde01

With Godot Physics the sphere/ball seems to just blink out of existence the moment it touches the first area, even without the increased subdivision (maybe because of the borked attenuation?), so there's not really a reference we can use here, but the simulation exploding is presumably not what we want.

Godot Physics does however seem a bit more well-behaved with pinned planar/non-pressurized soft bodies though, like in this scene for example, where you have two `PlaneMesh` subdivided 50x50: [soft_body_vs_sensor_2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24998457/soft_body_vs_sensor_2.zip)

Here's what it looks like with Jolt, with all properties at their defaults:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/907263df-8267-4416-b6b9-3bd38978bb3a

Here's what it looks like with Godot Physics, with all properties at their defaults:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8eb5f122-9681-4e71-a5e2-3166479637f3

Obviously parity is not really realistic, nor even desirable, given how broken much of the Godot Physics implementation of soft bodies seems to be, and perhaps there's something wrong about Godot Physics' behavior there that actually ends up "saving" it somehow, but do you think there's anything that can reasonably be done about the simulation exploding with Jolt in these cases?

> Note that this demo was seemingly created with the Jolt integration's current behavior in mind, so I wouldn't expect it to be well-behaved with Godot Physics. It's possible that we just need to change the demo a bit, by either increasing the total mass or reducing the subdivision a bit.

Running it with godot makes it explode. I've played around with the settings and it is indeed possible to make the demo work again by simply upping the total mass and reducing the some of the configured pressures, applied impulses etc. as they had been tweaked against the cloth with 63x63 subdivisions resulting in a 4 metric ton cloth (which is crazy considering that the UI says the cloth is 1 kg).

> With Godot Physics the sphere/ball seems to just blink out of existence the moment it touches the first area, even without the increased subdivision (maybe because of the borked attenuation?), so there's not really a reference we can use here, but the simulation exploding is presumably not what we want.

Yes, this is due to attenuation. If you disable it, it works. I specifically selected values to demonstrate the values for which Godot explodes.

> Obviously parity is not really realistic, nor even desirable, given how broken much of the Godot Physics implementation of soft bodies seems to be, and perhaps there's something wrong about Godot Physics' behavior there that actually ends up "saving" it somehow, but do you think there's anything that can reasonably be done about the simulation exploding with Jolt in these cases?

I'll look into this. I would expect to be able to run a 1 kg cloth simulating on its own.

> which is crazy considering that the UI says the cloth is 1 kg

I was curious as to why I felt comfortable defaulting the mass to 0 kg when the inspector ~~indeed shows 1~~ shows 0.001 kg, and it seems this changed in 4.6 somehow. In 4.5 and 4.4 it did in fact show the mass as 0[^1].

To give some more (messy) context, setting a mass of 0 on a `RigidBody3D` (which is not possible through `RigidBody3D` itself, but can still be done through the physics server[^2]) will similarly automatically calculate a mass for you when using Jolt, using whatever default your `JPH::Shape::GetMassProperties` returns, as seen [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/56f3e2611daadb0b1894b46737ee3000e82e33f9/modules/jolt_physics/objects/jolt_body_3d.cpp#L254). With Godot Physics it instead just throws an error, which seemed like a shame at the time, especially since Godot doesn't offer any way to automatically calculate the mass of an object in general.

When first implementing `SoftBody3D` in the extension I ran into similar issues of values adjusted for Godot's soft bodies not working very well and somehow found that this behavior of 1 kg per particle was at least stable, so I figured I'd just set the mass to 0 and treat that as "automatic" in the same way I had with `RigidBody3D`, albeit with a much worse heuristic. My thinking was that people who needed a specific mass would then hopefully note the weird default and tweak all of the properties in unison to something that worked for them.

In hindsight that was perhaps not the brightest idea, since 1 kg per particle is aggressive, and none of this was documented anywhere, so unsurprisingly led to the confusing situation we find ourselves in now.

[^1]: The fact that the `SoftBody3D` node even queries the physics server for these values to begin with is problematic. Scene nodes should always serve up cached values, or else they'll end up blocking the calling thread if the physics server runs on a different thread.
[^2]: Which, I'll admit, probably means nobody knows this exists, much less actually relying on it.

> when the inspector indeed shows 1

Out of curiosity, I was trying to bisect this change, and I think I managed to mix things up somehow, as I was only able to get it to show 1 kg by default again if I started the project with Godot Physics and then switched to Jolt Physics without restarting the editor (as prompted), in which case the editor would still be dealing with `GodotPhysicsServer3D` and all its soft body defaults. Perhaps you did the same thing?

Either way, there is still a new default value for `total_mass` shown in the inspector in 4.6-stable/4.7-dev, which is 0.001 kg, which seems to stem from #108758. ~~I guess with the reduced step size it no longer snaps down to 0 anymore, or something like that. Rightfully the inspector should never have shown 0 I guess, since the lower bound of that property was always non-zero.~~

Anyway, quite the mess, but the above comment still stands I guess.

I can confirm that it also unexplodes the [official soft body demo](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/3d/soft_body_physics) provided that:

* I set the sphere.tscn mass to 10 and the pressure to 100 (same as the box already had).
* I update the script to make the values better match a 1 kg cloth:

```
const WIND_FORCE: float = 100
const INTENSITY: float = 1
const INTENSITY: float = 0.1
```

> Either way, there is still a new default value for total_mass shown in the inspector in 4.6-stable/4.7-dev, which is 0.001 kg

I can reproduce this as well, but it happens only when Jolt is active. If you create a soft body it will show 0.001 kg, but if you then switch to godot physics (and restart) it shows 1 kg for that same body. If I update the default of `JoltSoftBody3D::mass` to 1.0f (like we did in the PR) then the attribute editor shows 1 kg. My guess the default 0.0 gets clamped to 0.001 because of 108758. Anyway, I don't think it matters as we clearly want to change the default to 1.0.

> In the meantime, I've made some good progress.

Wow, that looks really good!

I guess I shouldn't be surprised that my questionable compliance calculation came back to haunt us. I feel like we've touched almost every part of my original soft body integration at this point. 😅

> `// Calculate time step, assuming that we're running at 60 Hz`

I take it you want to use the actual engine time step there? You should be able to do something like:

```cpp
float physics_step = space->get_last_step();
if (physics_step <= 0.0f) {
	physics_step = 1.0f / Engine::get_singleton()->get_user_physics_ticks_per_second() * Engine::get_singleton()->get_effective_time_scale();
}
```

I'm not sure how we'd deal with the time scale though, since that unfortunately is something that can change at runtime (with no signal/notification) and affects the time by which the physics engine is stepped, as you can see there.

Also, I'm thinking we might want a separate pull request for the changes to the total mass and your new compliance calculation at this point. It's starting to feel a bit forced to cram that stuff into the area PR, and would make the breaking change a bit more focused.

> I can reproduce this as well, but it happens only when Jolt is active. If you create a soft body it will show 0.001 kg, but if you then switch to godot physics (and restart) it shows 1 kg for that same body. If I update the default of `JoltSoftBody3D::mass` to 1.0f (like we did in the PR) then the attribute editor shows 1 kg. My guess the default 0.0 gets clamped to 0.001 because of 108758. Anyway, I don't think it matters as we clearly want to change the default to 1.0.

Just to clarify, what I meant is that this 0.001 kg is purely cosmetic and specific to the inspector. The actual value being used is still 0 kg (without the pending PR). But yes, you're right, it doesn't really matter anymore.

> I take it you want to use the actual engine time step there? You should be able to do something like:

Yes, I didn't know how to get it but was sure you would correct me. Feel free to use your code in the PR :)

> I'm not sure how we'd deal with the time scale though, since that unfortunately is something that can change at runtime (with no signal/notification) and affects the time by which the physics engine is stepped, as you can see there.

I don't think we should listen to time scale. All we want to have is a mapping between stiffness and compliance and we wouldn't want the sim to suddenly become stiffer when time slows down.

> Also, I'm thinking we might want a separate pull request for the changes to the total mass and your new compliance calculation at this point. It's starting to feel a bit forced to cram that stuff into the area PR, and would make the breaking change a bit more focused.

Yes, I thought about suggesting the same. It would also make it easy to backport it to 4.6 (if we consider the mismatch between godot physics and Jolt in 4.6 a bug).

Edit: So maybe the delta time should always be `1.0f / Engine::get_singleton()->get_user_physics_ticks_per_second()` regardless of last time step / time scale.

> I don't think we should listen to time scale. All we want to have is a mapping between stiffness and compliance and we wouldn't want the sim to suddenly become stiffer when time slows down.

Gotcha.

> Yes, I thought about suggesting the same.

Feel free to create one.

> It would also make it easy to backport it to 4.6 (if we consider the mismatch between godot physics and Jolt in 4.6 a bug).

I'm not sure such a breaking change will be a popular addition to a patch release, but I do feel like it's better to rip this band-aid as soon as possible, especially with 4.6 being the first release with Jolt as default (for new projects). I'll ask around on monday to see what the policy is. It'd probably be good if we could get the PR up before then, since 4.6.1-rc1 is already out the door.

> So maybe the delta time should always be `1.0f / Engine::get_singleton()->get_user_physics_ticks_per_second()` regardless of last time step / time scale.

Yeah, that's probably fine. If we ever get the ability to step a physics space through the physics server API then that will be problematic though, but realistically most of these calls will likely happen before we've ever stepped the space anyway, in which case `JoltSpace3D::get_last_step()` will return 0 anyway, so it's whatever.

> Feel free to create one.

Ok, I'll create it. I'll also take a look at the influence of time scale while I'm at it.

I think it is a good decision not to take time scale into account. In godot physics this has a massive influence on the behavior of the cloth: With Jolt the sim is very comparable: You probably don't want your curtains to tense up if you activate bullet time...
The PR is up.

Hello,
I was wondering if there was any progress on this?
Are there other ways to apply wind physics besides the Area3D (which still does not work with jolt in 4.6) ?

Thanks

> I was wondering if there was any progress on this?

There's a pull request here, which ~~will most likely be~~ has been merged for 4.7-dev2: #114198

> Are there other ways to apply wind physics besides the Area3D

There's no ready-made helper for it, no, but you do have the `apply_force`/`apply_impulse` and `apply_central_force`/`apply_central_impulse` methods on `SoftBody3D`, which might help you achieve something similar.
